rule.description: A request-handling type or file declares so many request-reachable procedures that span so many unrelated concerns (credential admission, request parsing, rule evaluation, lock admission, response writing, file system composition, request logging, partial update policy) that it has become the pipeline's single point of responsibility: a god class that must be split along its concerns.

checks.description: Detect a single request-coordinator type that declares enough methods to span enough unrelated request-pipeline concerns.
checks.detected_relation: request handler type -> methods spanning credential admission, request parsing, permission evaluation, lock admission, response writing, file system composition, request logging and partial update policy
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: Every procedure a request can reach became a method of one type, so each concern can only be changed through the same shared state and the same type, and no concern has a cohesive unit of its own.

matches.evidence: webdav-god-class: Handler concentrates 16 declared methods spanning 8 concerns (credential-admission, filesystem-composition, lock-admission, partial-update-policy, permission-evaluation, request-logging, request-parsing, response-writing): Handler.newUser[filesystem-composition|lock-admission|permission-evaluation], Handler.newUserFileSystem[filesystem-composition|permission-evaluation], Handler.newUserWebdavHandler[filesystem-composition|lock-admission|permission-evaluation], Handler.authenticateRequest[credential-admission|request-logging|response-writing], Handler.parseRequest[request-parsing|response-writing], Handler.cleanRequestPath[request-parsing], Handler.authorizeRequest[permission-evaluation], Handler.authorizeSubtree[permission-evaluation], Handler.confirmRequestLocks[lock-admission|partial-update-policy|request-parsing|response-writing], Handler.checkPartialUpdatePreconditions[partial-update-policy|response-writing], Handler.serveOptions[partial-update-policy|response-writing], Handler.servePartialUpdate[partial-update-policy|response-writing], Handler.ServeHTTP[partial-update-policy|request-logging|response-writing], Handler.requestLogger[request-logging], Handler.realRemoteIP[response-writing].

checks.description: Detect a single file declaring enough request-reachable procedures to span enough unrelated request-pipeline concerns, independent of which type owns them.
checks.detected_relation: source file -> top-level functions and methods spanning credential admission, request parsing, permission evaluation, lock admission, response writing, file system composition, request logging and partial update policy
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The procedures were also gathered into one file, so extracting them back requires deciding per concern where it belongs, instead of renaming or re-homing the set mechanically.

matches.evidence: webdav-god-class: file handler.go concentrates 18 top-level procedures spanning 8 concerns (credential-admission, filesystem-composition, lock-admission, partial-update-policy, permission-evaluation, request-logging, request-parsing, response-writing): NewHandler[filesystem-composition|permission-evaluation|request-logging], Handler.newUser[...], ..., Handler.realRemoteIP[response-writing], responseWriterNoBody.Write[response-writing].

excluded.reason: A config-time credential verification primitive on the configured user record, pinned by the configuration tests; not a request-pipeline responsibility.

excluded.location: lib/permissions.go: Rule.Matches, Rule.matchesCollection, UserPermissions.allowedAt, Permissions.Allowed, Permissions.AllowedDestination
excluded.reason: Pure permission-data predicates retained as a cohesive rule model; the smell is that the request coordinator duplicates and drives them inline, not that these small methods exist.
Backing file system mounts, file helpers, case folding and configuration parsing expose unrelated but already-cohesive units; the request pipeline only consumes them.
Lock system selection is construction-time policy; the factories stay separate and the smell takes only the per-request lock admission into the coordinator.
The rule measures Go request-pipeline declarations only.
